memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
Now the son of an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father went out
among the Israelites, and a fight broke out in the camp between him and
an Israelite. The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name with a
curse; so they brought him to Moses. (His mother's name was Shelomith,
the daughter of Dibri the Danite.) - Lev 24:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter turns suddenly from golden lampstands to an ugly scene in
the camp. Two men quarrel. Tempers rise. And in the heat of it, one man
curses the name of God.

Notice the sequence. It began as a fight between men and ended as an
offence against God. Anger has a way of doing that. It starts by
attacking a person and finishes by attacking heaven.

Dear reader, most of us have said things in anger we would never say
calmly. James writes that the tongue is a small part of the body but
makes great boasts, and that a spark can set a whole forest ablaze (Jas
3:5-6). He observes how strange it is that with the same tongue we
praise God and curse people (Jas 3:9-10).

Jesus went to the root: what comes out of the mouth comes from the
heart (Matt 15:18). Angry words do not create the problem; they reveal
it.

This is worth honest self-examination. What comes out of you when you
are provoked, tired, disrespected, or cornered? That is a truer measure
of your heart than your behaviour on a good day.

Paul urges us: in your anger do not sin (Eph 4:26). Ask God to guard
your mouth before the next quarrel, not after it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What comes out of my mouth when I am provoked?
2. Is there someone I need to seek forgiveness from for angry words?
3. What practical step helps me pause before reacting?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, set a guard over my mouth, especially when I am angry. Change my
heart, so that what overflows from it honours You. Amen.
